knowledge:
- key_parameters: path=The path to the directory containing cohort sub-folders with Picard txt or BAM files ;; order=A character vector specifying the factor levels/order of cohorts along the plot axes ;; limit=A numeric vector of length 2 specifying the fragment size range (e.g., c(50, 135)) for peak/valley distance calculations ;; mode_partition=A list specifying how to group/stratify modes in plotModeSummary ;; vline=A parameter in plotSingleGroup to control vertical lines (can be set to NULL to disable default lines)
- alternatives: Picard CollectInsertSizeMetrics is mentioned as the standard upstream command-line tool used to generate the input insert size metrics text files.
- when_to_use: Use this package when analyzing cfDNA whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data (specifically Illumina NGS data) to characterize fragment size distributions, identify 10bp periodic oscillations, and compare fragmentation metrics (like median size, modal size, and peak/valley distances) across multiple cohorts or samples.
- pitfalls: Input files (Picard txt or BAM) must be organized into sub-folders named by cohort name, even if there is only one cohort in the study ;; BAM files must be Illumina NGS data and must meet specific criteria: proper pair flag, mapping quality >= 30, and CIGAR string without "I" or "D" ;; Fragment sizes below 30bp are noisy and above 500bp are too low to be useful, so the default analysis focuses on the 30bp-500bp range.

workflows.name: single_cohort_analysis
workflows.intent: Characterize and visualize fragment size distribution (proportions and cumulative distribution functions) for a single cohort.
input: data_path (directory containing sub-folders named by cohort, each containing Picard insert size metrics .txt files or BAM files)
workflows.stages: 1. Retrieve the path to the input data directory using examplePath ;; 2. Extract fragment size distribution data using callSize ;; 3. Filter the dataset for the target cohort ;; 4. Generate proportion and cumulative distribution plots using plotSingleGroup
workflows.code:
data_path <- examplePath("groups_picard")
cohort1_plot <- cfDNAPro::callSize(path = data_path) %>%
  dplyr::filter(group == as.character("cohort_1")) %>%
  cfDNAPro::plotSingleGroup()

workflows.name: multi_cohort_comparison
workflows.intent: Compare median size metrics, modal fragment sizes, and inter-peak/valley distances across multiple cohorts.
input: data_path (directory containing sub-folders named by cohort, each containing Picard insert size metrics .txt files or BAM files)
workflows.stages: 1. Calculate and plot median size metrics across cohorts using callMetrics and plotMetrics ;; 2. Calculate and plot modal fragment sizes using callMode, plotMode, and plotModeSummary ;; 3. Calculate and plot inter-peak distances using callPeakDistance and plotPeakDistance ;; 4. Calculate and plot inter-valley distances using callValleyDistance and plotValleyDistance
workflows.code:
data_path <- examplePath("groups_picard")
order <- c("cohort_1", "cohort_2", "cohort_3", "cohort_4")
compare_grps<-callMetrics(data_path) %>% plotMetrics(order=order)

mode_bin <- callMode(data_path) %>% plotMode(order=order,hline = c(167,111,81))

mode_stacked <- 
  callMode(data_path) %>% 
  plotModeSummary(order=order,
                  mode_partition = list(c(166,167)))

inter_peak_dist<-callPeakDistance(path = data_path,  limit = c(50, 135)) %>%
  plotPeakDistance(order = order)

inter_valley_dist<-callValleyDistance(path = data_path,  
                                      limit = c(50, 135)) %>%
  plotValleyDistance(order = order)

workflows.name: peak_valley_highlighting
workflows.intent: Identify and visually highlight specific peak and valley locations on a single sample's fragmentation pattern.
input: exam_path (directory containing Picard insert size metrics .txt files or BAM files for a specific sample)
workflows.stages: 1. Calculate peak distances using callPeakDistance ;; 2. Calculate valley distances using callValleyDistance ;; 3. Generate the base fragmentation pattern plot using callSize and plotSingleGroup ;; 4. Overlay peak and valley locations as vertical lines or dots using ggplot2 layers
workflows.code:
exam_path <- examplePath("step6")
peaks <- callPeakDistance(path = exam_path) 
valleys <- callValleyDistance(path = exam_path) 
exam_plot_all <- callSize(path=exam_path) %>% plotSingleGroup(vline = NULL)
exam_plot_prop <- exam_plot_all$prop + 
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(90,135),ylim = c(0,0.0065)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept=peaks$insert_size, colour="red",linetype="dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = valleys$insert_size,colour="blue")

exam_plot_prop_dot<- exam_plot_all$prop + 
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(90,135),ylim = c(0,0.0065)) +
  geom_point(data= peaks, 
             mapping = aes(x= insert_size, y= prop),
             color="blue",alpha=0.5,size=3) +
  geom_point(data= valleys, 
             mapping = aes(x= insert_size, y= prop),
             color="red",alpha=0.5,size=3)
